mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate directly lowers discount rates for equity valuation models, increasing the present value of future cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth indicates robust economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and investor confidence, which drives sustained positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth above 2.0% quarterly fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase exceeding 3.5% year-over-year indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months with CPIAUCSL YoY growth above 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production and housing starts signal a contraction in the real economy, triggering sharp reductions in corporate demand for capital goods and consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both INDPRO and HOUST decline.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in retail sales and housing starts indicate strong consumer and business confidence, driving sustained economic growth and corporate earnings, which produce positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST rise.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a monthly payroll growth decline below 100,000 jobs signals the end of the labor market boom, reducing consumer spending and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances in late-cycle expansion when PAYEMS change < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock, a decline in industrial production below 100 (index 2017=100) indicates reduced manufacturing output, suppressing corporate profits and investor sentiment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 100.0 during a supply shock.
